currentContext.business: The Company operates three reported business verticals - Products, Solutions and Real Estate - supported by a Service Business Unit that acts as the operations arm for maintenance, operations and repair of all OEM products it sells. The Products unit sells indigenous routers, switches, Unified Threat Manager appliances and data-centre networking platforms to Telecom, Broadband, Enterprise, Government, Public Sector, Railways and Defence customers, while the Solutions unit manages, operates and maintains turnkey network projects across the country through Network Operations Centres. The Real Estate vertical develops premium residential projects, with UmiyaBricklane at Candolim, North Goa, and Umiya Prism on Cunningham Road, Bengaluru, launched by the associated firm Umiya Buildtek.

Products: High-performance switching platforms on disaggregated architecture with SONiC Network Operating System
TDMoIP device (Network Interface Unit) for defence
Integrated Private 5G solution (Radio Unit, Centralised/Distributed Unit, Core Network, Network Management platform)
Solutions: Network Operations Centre (NOC) based network management services
Operations and maintenance of network projects
Services: Maintenance, operations and repair of all OEM products sold by the Company
Real Estate: Umiya Prism, Cunningham Road, Bengaluru (launched by associated firm Umiya Buildtek)

currentContext.expansion: Expansion during FY 2025-26 was led by the Real Estate vertical and by indigenous manufacturing and R&D build-out rather than by a conventional plant capex programme; the Company states it undertook strategic initiatives towards expanding its presence in next-generation technologies, strengthening its real estate portfolio, enhancing indigenous manufacturing capabilities and increasing focus on research and development. In real estate, UmiyaBricklane at Candolim, North Goa - the Company's strategic expansion into a high-potential tourism and lifestyle destination - secured all key regulatory approvals including RERA registration and plan approvals and drew an encouraging market response with initial bookings and customer advances; the associated firm Umiya Buildtek launched Umiya Prism on Cunningham Road, Bengaluru, an ultra-luxury boutique residential project in the Central Business District, which has received RERA approval and where initial project development activities are currently underway. On the manufacturing side, the Company has commenced R&D on an indigenous 1G switch: firmware development is in progress and the switch hardware will be run from a Completely Knocked Down (CKD) kit and manufactured at the Company's own factory, with roll-out expected at more than 65% local content. The Solutions footprint covers 5 projects managed, operated and maintained across the country, operating nearly 1500 links with four Network Operations Centres, extended during the year by an additional order of 50 sites under the Pondicherry SWAN project and an order from RailTel for supply of TDM/IP devices for a key Railways project. The Company also disposed of its property at Electronic City during the year, and states that the coming year's focus will be on greater hiring and R&D effort.

risks.note: Listed as a threat in the Company's own SWOT analysis. The Products and Solutions businesses sell largely into Telecom PSUs, Government, Public Sector, Railways, Defence and state networks (Pondicherry SWAN, BSNL-WCL, BSNL-BCCL, RailTel-WCL, APEPDCL), so revenue is tied to public tendering, budget cycles and policy continuity.
Listed as a threat in the SWOT analysis; customer liquidity constraints stretch collections and working capital in a tender-driven, project-based business.

Listed as a weakness in the SWOT analysis. Product engineering, firmware and network integration depend on scarce specialist talent, which is why management says the coming year's focus will be greater hiring.
Listed as a weakness in the SWOT analysis; expensive funding weighs on a business that must fund R&D, inventory and project execution as well as real estate development.
Management itself flags R&D as a weakness even while new products (1G indigenous switch, NOS, UTM, SD-WAN) are the stated growth engine, so under-investment directly threatens the product roadmap.

risks.risk: Increased market competition in networking products
risks.note: The Company notes it maintained product sales 'despite increased market competition and various challenges', indicating competitive pressure on the switching and routing business.

risks.risk: Contract renewal and renegotiation risk in the Solutions business
risks.note: Solutions revenue declined because projects were in the renewal and contract renegotiation stage during the year, showing that recurring O&M revenue is exposed to re-tendering and repricing at contract expiry.

risks.risk: Dependence on certifications and trusted-source status for market access
risks.note: Market acceptance rests on TEC certification, clearing RDSO inspection and remaining a Trusted Source on the DoT Trusted Portal, plus compliance with the National Security Directive on the Telecommunication Sector; loss or non-renewal of any of these would restrict access to the Company's core public-sector markets.
